question: Did mainnet change to Qwen/Qwen3-14B at block 3500, and do its blocks reach a GREEN Full verdict like the blocks before?
method: analysis/model_switch_mainnet.py read every block from the public explorer API, from 144 blocks before the switch height in mainnet/network.json to the tip, and summarised each side of the switch: the model each proof names, Full verdicts, seconds from block time to the GREEN verdict, output tokens, reward addresses and intervals.
findings: All 69 blocks from 3500 to 3568 name Qwen/Qwen3-14B@40c069824f4251a91eefaf281ebe4c544efd3e18; all 144 blocks before name Qwen3-0.6B at its pinned revision.
All 69 blocks after the switch have a GREEN Full verdict; none was RED or still waiting when read.
Block to GREEN verdict after the switch: median 306 s, p90 336 s, max 416 s; before it: median 65.5 s.
One reward address produced every block after the switch (8 addresses in the 144 blocks before).
notEstablished: Sustained operation: 69 blocks over about 8.1 hours, not days or weeks.
More than one 14B miner: a single reward address has mined since the switch, so other hardware and setups are not shown on mainnet.
Independent verification: one verifier, run by the same operator, replayed every block.
A forged or wrong 14B proof refused on mainnet: no RED block since the switch; refusal is covered only by the offline rehearsal (model-switch-rehearsal.json).
Why time to final rose about fivefold, and whether that matters to users; the record measures it, it does not explain it.
Miner and verifier hardware, memory and cost: not visible from the chain.
